name: Worm Selector
summary: On a desktop, the user draws free-form contours on a movable drawing plane; successive contours are joined into a tube-like envelope (the worm), and all points inside it are selected.
howItWorks: The drawing plane is positioned and oriented separately from the camera; the camera can then turn to face it, and the user draws a closed contour of any shape with the mouse around the visible cross-section of the target. Each new contour, possibly at a different angle, is resampled to 360 points and linked point by point to the previous one, extending the envelope section by section; deleting a contour removes its section. In a study with 12 participants selecting irregular volumes in point clouds, it was significantly faster than a Sphere/Cuboid selector built from adjustable primitives, with similar precision and recall, and was preferred. It performed like a Parallel Contours variant restricted to parallel planes.
limitations: Twisted or folded envelopes can be hard to understand.
Many contours are needed for complex shapes.

relationships.note: Both build a selection volume from contours drawn on the screen.
